title: Paint all five fingernails of a manicure practice hand with red polish, keeping it off the skin
instruction: Paint all five fingernails of the practice hand with the red polish, keeping it off the skin, then put the brush back in the bottle.
context: Painting nails is an everyday grooming act that many people do themselves and almost everyone has watched up close, at home or at a nail salon. The brush is the bottle's cap: dipped for each nail, it is laid on at an angle and drawn from just short of the cuticle out past the free edge in two or three side-by-side strokes, so each 9-13 mm nail is coated edge to edge while the skin round it stays clean.
setup: Table; cm from the arm-base midpoint (x forward, y left), heights above the table. A white folded towel (26 x 20 x 0.6) centred (35.5, -15). On it a soft practice hand (28.4 cm overall, skin-coloured, held by its table clamp): a right hand palm down, fingers spread and pointing at the robot, thumb on the robot's right; knuckle line at x 33.5, palm 9 x 8.6 x 2.2 thick spanning y -18.8 to -10.2; fingertips at x 25.7-27.7 (thumb tip at (35, -22)). Bare nails, pale pink: thumb 11.5 x 12.5 mm, index 11 x 10.5, middle 11.5 x 11, ring 11 x 10.5, little 9 x 8.5 (length x width). A 13.5 mL bottle of red polish (essie original: 2.9 x 2.9 cm glass body, 9 cm tall with its cap) in a rubber holder taped at (21.5, -25.5), closed: its cap-brush (cap 1.6 cm dia x 3.6 cm, 3 mm stem, flat bristle tuft about 6 x 2 x 10 mm) seated on the neck. Polish filled to 3.6 cm deep in the bottle (about 70% full), topped up before each trial. Trial cameras: a scene camera and a close-up phone fixed about 25 cm above the hand framing all five fingertips.
scoring: Score 0 if polish touches skin more than 1 mm outside any nail's edge at any time. Otherwise, from an end photo of the nails through a 0.5 mm grid overlay: 0.18 for each nail with at least 90% of its area coated, 0.09 if 50-90%. Plus 0.10 if at least one nail scored, the cap is seated back on the bottle's neck (within 10 degrees of upright, 5 mm of its axis and 3 mm of the neck top), and both grippers are 10 cm or more from the brush, bottle and hand, and still (under 2 cm/s) for 0.5 s. 1.0 = all five nails coated, brush home, hands parked.
reset_notes: Remove the polish with acetone and cotton pads and dry the nails; fit fresh nitrile finger cots on the gripper pads; check the hand is clamped at its tape marks with the fingers spread as in the setup photo; seat the cap on the bottle (not screwed); bottle in its holder on its paper sheet.
fidelity: Rigid hand, flat nail plates (real nails curve slightly); hand fixed as by its clamp. Brush one rigid body, all of it colliding. Polish not simulated as liquid: dipping the tuft below the polish level inside the bottle loads about one nail's worth (160 mm2); a nail is coated only while the physics engine reports the loaded tuft pressing on it (over 0.02 N), over 1.2 mm round each lowest-edge point on the plate (bristle splay). Cap seats on the neck, not screwed. Brush size approximate.
